mechanism: A strong leader appends ordered commands, commits after a quorum, and applies one deterministic state machine to every replica.
why_great: The safety story is one ordered log and one deterministic apply path; a common command completes after one majority round under healthy timing.
jet_evidence: docs/plans/epoch-3/universal-language-core.md:199 (#444 fault-tolerant distributed service runtime); probes/help.out lists no raft/consensus command
needed: Provide a production replicated-log building block with durable recovery, quorum commit, and explicit transport and storage seams.

mechanism: Candidates use randomized election timeouts, RequestVote RPCs, and a strong leader that renews authority through heartbeats.
why_great: The protocol has one visible authority and simple terms; failure becomes a bounded election rather than application-level arbitration.
jet_evidence: docs/plans/epoch-3/universal-language-core.md:199; probes/help.out has no consensus runtime
needed: Supply election, term, heartbeat, quorum-loss, and leader-transfer behavior with observable failure reasons.

mechanism: Configuration changes first use overlapping majorities, then switch to the new membership without a split-brain gap.
why_great: Membership is a protocol state transition, not an operator hope; old and new quorums overlap during the change.
jet_evidence: docs/plans/epoch-3/universal-language-core.md:199; no membership/consensus source found in Source/crates/examples
needed: Support safe add, remove, replace, and recover membership with proof of overlapping quorums.

mechanism: Replicas compact committed prefixes into snapshots and install snapshots when a follower is too far behind.
why_great: Long-lived clusters do not retain an unbounded log; catch-up has a defined snapshot path.
jet_evidence: docs/plans/epoch-3/universal-language-core.md:199; no Raft snapshot implementation in Source/crates/examples
needed: Add bounded snapshot creation, durable install, recovery, and compaction observability.

mechanism: The core accepts a Message and returns messages, log entries, and next state; identical state and input produce identical output.
why_great: The algorithm core is deterministic and leaves I/O to the host, which makes tests, replay, and alternate transports straightforward.
jet_evidence: docs/spec/proof-replay-decisions.md:1-25 is a general proof/replay law, but no Raft Message state machine exists
needed: Expose a deterministic consensus core whose state transition can be recorded and replayed independently of network and disk.

feature: Ready boundary for persistence and transport
mechanism: Node.Ready yields entries, messages, snapshots, and hard state; the host persists and sends them, then calls Advance.
why_great: The library stays small and deterministic while the application owns network, disk, batching, and backpressure decisions.
jet_evidence: docs/spec/architecture.md:748-754 gives tier parity but no consensus Ready/storage seam
needed: Provide explicit durable-storage, outbound-message, apply, snapshot, and acknowledgement boundaries.

mechanism: Quorum read-only requests preserve linearizability; lease reads trade clock assumptions for lower overhead.
why_great: The expert can choose a correctness-preserving quorum path or a documented latency tradeoff instead of an accidental stale read.
evidence: https://github.com/etcd-io/raft README (linearizable read-only queries; lease-based reads)
jet_evidence: docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:3898-3921 has no consensus read mode; probes/help.out has no distributed read command
needed: Expose consistency mode, clock assumptions, and quorum evidence in read operations.

mechanism: Transactions atomically read and write an ordered key-value space across a replicated cluster.
why_great: The application gets serializable transaction semantics while layers remain stateless and composable.
jet_evidence: docs/spec/spec.md:645-679 only covers local #Transact rollback and irreversible effects; no distributed database transaction
needed: Provide a durable distributed transaction substrate with conflict detection, retry policy, and recovery evidence.

mechanism: Byte-string keys sort lexicographically; transactions support key selectors, range reads, and range clears.
why_great: Ordered primitives build indexes, scans, and locality without a separate query planner or hidden database type.
jet_evidence: docs/spec/feature-claims.json:1678-1680 mentions core.net/http, not an ordered distributed KV API; no FoundationDB-like API in crates/examples
needed: Ship an ordered durable KV interface with bounded range selection and clear semantics.

mechanism: Subspace and tuple packing create structured key namespaces; directories and tenants organize those namespaces.
why_great: The layer avoids hand-built prefixes while preserving raw ordered-key performance and composability.
jet_evidence: No Subspace/Tuple/Directory/Tenant implementation found in Source/crates/examples; probes/help.out has no database namespace command
needed: Support typed namespacing and tenant isolation over the ordered store without forcing string prefix conventions.

mechanism: Higher-level layers implement records, directories, and indexes over the same transactional ordered KV core.
why_great: A small trusted core can grow capabilities without coupling every feature to a new storage engine.
jet_evidence: docs/plans/epoch-3/universal-language-core.md:165 lists data platforms as future compute territory; no distributed KV layer seam
needed: Make storage extensions composable and stateless over one transactional authority.

mechanism: Flow and Simulation run real cluster code in a deterministic single-threaded simulated time environment with network, machine, disk, and datacenter faults.
why_great: The same code sees controlled partitions and failures, so rare schedules can be reproduced instead of guessed at in production.
jet_evidence: docs/spec/proof-replay-decisions.md:1-25 ratifies proof/replay artifacts but not a cluster simulator; docs/plans/epoch-3/universal-language-core.md:199 names distributed runtime as future
needed: Add deterministic cluster simulation that runs the actual service and records faults, schedule, state, and replay identity.

mechanism: Circus runs large parallel/sequential workloads while simulation and hardware-failure tests exercise correctness and throughput separately.
why_great: Correctness faults and throughput regressions are measured with the same workload shape instead of mixing a toy benchmark with a production claim.
jet_evidence: gauntlet/matrix.json and gauntlet/measurement-manifest.json contain no FoundationDB, consensus, or distributed-systems cell
needed: Add a repeatable correctness-plus-performance harness with workload, fault, hardware, and output identity recorded.

mechanism: Replicas edit local copies offline and merge concurrent changes without coordination or lost work.

mechanism: Automerge retains change history and supports old versions, diffs, branches, and merges as first-class document operations.

mechanism: Repo accepts multiple NetworkAdapters, including WebSocket, MessageChannel, and BroadcastChannel transports.

mechanism: Y.encodeStateAsUpdate produces a binary update and Y.applyUpdate applies it; update order does not affect convergence.

mechanism: A small state-based Awareness CRDT propagates JSON presence, user, cursor, and online/offline state without persisting it in the document.

mechanism: Providers include y-indexeddb, y-leveldb, and y-redis, letting the same CRDT update model target browser, local, and server storage.

mechanism: SyncCounter uses per-replica positive/negative maxima; SyncMap uses deterministic clock/writer resolution; SyncList and generic forms preserve Codable values.

mechanism: Automerge tracks causal history and Yjs tracks update state vectors; those structures distinguish seen operations from merely ordered operations.

mechanism: app.sync publishes a canonical CRDT document to a named session; duplicate delivery returns the existing generation and changed state publishes through the live transport.

mechanism: Nodes read JSON messages from stdin, write responses to stdout, and log diagnostics to stderr while Maelstrom simulates the network.

mechanism: Maelstrom renders timelines, message statistics, time-series graphs, and Lamport diagrams from a test run.

mechanism: Each request carries a client-generated unique u128 id; the database promises strict serializability and at-most-once processing.

jet_evidence: docs/spec/spec.md:645-679 gives atomic local Shared/#Transact only; no distributed strict-serializable store or u128 request identity

mechanism: VOPR runs the real cluster under network, storage, and process faults in a deterministic simulated world and can replay failures.

mechanism: The hot path batches up to 8,190 transfers/queries, pipelines I/O, uses cache-aligned fixed records, and keeps one leader core per node.

mechanism: A proto3 schema declares messages and services; protoc plus a gRPC plugin generates typed client and server stubs across languages.

jet_evidence: docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:602-615 has typed local protocols but no proto3/protoc/gRPC surface; examples/features/concurrency/protocol.jet is in-process only

mechanism: A call returns a promise whose methods can be passed into another call, collapsing dependent remote operations into one round trip.

jet_evidence: docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:602-615 only gives local typed protocol typestate; no remote promise/capability implementation

mechanism: Capability references are first-class parameters and fields; possession grants permission and disconnects surface as typed failure.

feature: Paxos majority safety and stable storage
mechanism: Prepare and accept phases use majority acceptors; stable storage preserves promises and accepted values across restart.

mechanism: Channels move sendable owned values; mutable captures, views, and Cells are rejected across task and channel boundaries.
